results.title: Banana Phone: The $50 Banana That Outlived Its Own Punchline | YesPress
results.content:
## 05 / Shark TankFive nos, and a good year anyway

In 2022 the founders took the Banana Phone onto Shark Tank's fourteenth season and asked for $250,000 in exchange for 10% of the company - a $2.5 million valuation. They walked in with real numbers: roughly $545,000 in sales the prior year and about $123,000 in profit. And they walked out with nothing. Barbara Corcoran and Kevin O'Leary were put off that the founders would not quit their day jobs; Mark Cuban and Lori Greiner simply passed; Robert Herjavec enjoyed the pitch but doubted the growth. Five nos.

 

The pitch, on paper. Profitable, growing slowly, and unwilling to bet the founders' careers on it - a combination sharks rarely reward but customers did not care about. # The $50 Banana That Outlived Its Own Punchline [...] The slow banana curve. A crowdfunding spark in 2017, a genuinely profitable 2021, a Shark Tank bump in 2022, and past $1.6M cumulative by 2023. Figures are approximate and drawn from public reporting.

 

## 03 / The problem it solvesTwo markets, one banana

The clever part of the business is that it sells into two markets at once. The impulse-buy novelty market is enormous and forgiving, but usually punishing on the back end - most gag gadgets die on a clearance rack within a season. The screen-time and wellness market is more durable but crowded with earnest, joyless products. The Banana Phone straddles both. It is funny enough to sell as a gift and functional enough to keep, which is why it did not follow the usual novelty arc into the bargain bin.
